Learning Pathway: Generating a new pathway from a valid own exam attempt succeeds and archives any prior ACTIVE pathway, enforcing the single-active-pathway rule.
column3:
1. Log in as a learner who already has an ACTIVE pathway from a prior generation.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/pathways/generate body {"examAttemptId":<own attempt>}.
3. Send the request and inspect the response's nodes[]/weak_skills[].
4. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/pathways/me to confirm the old pathway is now archived.
column4:
1. Step 3: 200 OK; LearningPathwayResponseDTO with nodes[], weak_skills[], etc.
2. Step 4: returns the NEW pathway; the old one is now status=ARCHIVED, confirming the single-active-pathway invariant.
column5: - Logged in learner with ENROLL_AND_LEARN_COURSES; owns a completed exam attempt; already has one ACTIVE pathway from before.

Learning Pathway: A node's returned status is recomputed live from actual lesson-completion data on every read, so it can auto-promote from LOCKED without any pathway-specific mutation call.
column3:
1. Log in and note a LOCKED node's underlying course and its lessons.
2. Prepare and send PUT /api/v1/lessons/{id}/complete for one of that course's lessons — an action completely unrelated to the pathway API.
3. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/pathways/{id} again.
4. Inspect that node's status field.
column4: 1. Step 3-4: the node's status has changed to IN_PROGRESS (or COMPLETED at 100%) purely because of the out-of-band lesson completion — no pathway mutation call was made.
column5: - A LOCKED node whose course has at least one completable lesson.

Learning Pathway: Rerouting appears to unconditionally re-lock all downstream (non-completed) nodes regardless of whether the latest exam score was good or bad — verify this holds even for a HIGH-scoring student, where the messaging implies "no action needed."
column3:
1. Log in and arrange the caller's most recent exam attempt to score ≥60.
2. Note the current status of every downstream (non-completed) node in the pathway.
3. Prepare and send PUT /api/v1/pathways/{id}/reroute.
4. Inspect the mentor summary text AND re-check every downstream node's status/progress for any changes.
column4: 1. Step 3-4: 200 OK; mentor summary says the plan is fine, BUT the node-locking loop still runs — confirm whether downstream nodes are still reset/locked despite the "no changes needed" messaging (documents a possible mismatch between text and actual state mutation).
column5: - Own pathway with a recent exam attempt scoring ≥60.

Learning Pathway: Applying a valid schedule computes per-node hours from each course's lesson count and builds a backwards calendar toward the target date.
column3:
1. Log in with an own pathway containing ≥1 node.
2. Prepare PUT /api/v1/pathways/{id}/schedule body {"goalName":"Band 6.5","targetDate":"<a date ~8 weeks out>","hoursPerWeek":10,"preferredStudyDays":[1,3,5]}.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect each node's start_date/deadline/estimated_hours and the overall schedule_status.
column4: 1. 200 OK; schedule_status="ON_TRACK"; each node has start_date/deadline/estimated_hours populated (estimated_hours = lessonCount×2, or 3 if the course has zero lessons).
column5: - Own pathway with ≥1 node.

Learning Pathway: A schedule's BEHIND/ON_TRACK status is computed once at apply-time and does NOT auto-recompute later, so a schedule that was ON_TRACK when applied keeps reporting ON_TRACK even after its deadline silently passes.
column3:
1. Log in and apply a schedule with a target date just 1-2 days in the future (so it reports ON_TRACK at apply time).
2. Wait until that date has passed (or simulate a clock advance in a test environment).
3. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/pathways/{id} again WITHOUT re-applying any schedule.
4. Inspect the node's scheduleStatus.
column4: 1. Step 3-4: nodes still show scheduleStatus="ON_TRACK" from the original apply-time computation, even though their deadlines are now in the past — confirms this field is NOT recomputed on every read (contrast with node status/progress, which IS recomputed live per PATHWAY_FT09).
column5: - A schedule applied with a target date that will pass within the test window.

Learning Pathway: Accepting a FAST_TRACK suggestion correctly marks the node skipped and writes an audit event; accepting a DETOUR_REQUIRED suggestion instead inserts the pathway's FIRST course as a "remedial" step regardless of what skill is actually weak.
column3:
1. Obtain a FAST_TRACK_ELIGIBLE suggestion (per PATHWAY_FT21), then prepare and send POST /api/v1/pathways/{id}/reroute/accept; inspect the resulting node and audit log.
2. Separately, obtain a DETOUR_REQUIRED suggestion (per PATHWAY_FT20), then prepare and send POST /api/v1/pathways/{id}/reroute/accept; inspect the newly inserted node.
3. Compare the inserted "remedial" course's identity against the pathway's very first course.
column4:
1. Step 1: 200 OK; the target node becomes status=COMPLETED, nodeType=FAST_TRACK_SKIPPED, isOptional=true; the next LOCKED node unlocks; a PathwayEvent audit record is written.
2. Step 2: 200 OK; a new "remedial" node is inserted that is literally a copy of the pathway's own FIRST course — even if that course has nothing to do with the actual failing skill — subsequent nodes shift down by one stepOrder; a PathwayEvent is also written.
column5: - Suggestions obtained per PATHWAY_FT20/21 respectively.

Learning Pathway: Declining a suggestion is a pure no-op, so the identical suggestion reappears immediately on the next check.
column3:
1. Log in and obtain a pending suggestion via POST /api/v1/pathways/{id}/reroute/suggestions.
2. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/pathways/{id}/reroute/decline.
3. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/pathways/{id}/reroute/suggestions again.
4. Compare the second suggestion's node_type/reason against the first.
column4:
1. Step 2: 200 OK, just re-returns the current pathway state.
2. Step 3-4: the SAME suggestion (same node_type/reason) is returned again — nothing was recorded to suppress it.
column5: - A pending suggestion exists as of step 1.

Learning Pathway: Sending a non-numeric hoursPerWeek inside the ADJUST_SCHEDULE payload throws an unguarded cast exception, surfacing as a masked 500.
column3:
1. Log in with an own pathway that already has a targetDate/hoursPerWeek set.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/pathways/{id}/mentor-action body {"actionType":"ADJUST_SCHEDULE","payload":{"hoursPerWeek":"ten"}} (a string instead of a number).
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response status.
column4: 1. 500 Internal Server Error — the unguarded ((Number) payload.get("hoursPerWeek")).intValue() cast throws a ClassCastException for a non-numeric JSON value.
column5: - Own pathway exists, ideally already has a targetDate/hoursPerWeek set.

Learning Pathway: An ordinary off-topic question that matches neither the "learning" nor the "off-topic" keyword lists is treated as in-scope by default and forwarded to the live LLM — a looser guardrail than the lesson-level AI Assistant's embedding-based check.
column3:
1. Log in with an own pathway.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/pathways/{id}/chat body {"message":"What's 2+2?"} (a message matching neither keyword list).
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response's was_out_of_scope flag and reply content.
column4: 1. 200 OK; was_out_of_scope=false — the message is forwarded to the live LLM despite arguably being off-topic, since the keyword pre-filter only catches a short hardcoded list (bitcoin/crypto/weather/recipe/football/etc.).
column5: - Logged in; own pathway exists.

3. Send the request.

Learning Pathway: Chat history spanning multiple conversation threads is NOT in strict chronological order — it's newest-conversation-first, chronological within each thread, which can look like a confusing jump backward in time.
column3:
1. Log in and trigger creation of a second conversation thread for the same pathway (e.g. via PATHWAY_FT28's bogus-id trick), so two threads now exist.
2. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/pathways/{id}/chat/history.
3. Inspect the ordering of messages across the two threads in the response.
column4: 1. The returned list shows the newest conversation's messages first (oldest-to-newest within it), THEN jumps back to the older conversation's messages (also oldest-to-newest within it) — not one single global chronological timeline.
column5: - ≥2 conversation threads exist for the same pathway.

Learning Pathway: Clearing chat history deletes every conversation thread for the pathway in a single call — there is no way to delete just one thread.
column3:
1. Log in and ensure ≥2 conversation threads exist for the pathway.
2. Prepare and send DELETE /api/v1/pathways/{id}/chat/history.
3. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/pathways/{id}/chat/history again.
4. Inspect the returned list to confirm it is now empty.
column4:
1. Step 2: 200 OK, empty body.
2. Step 3-4: returns an empty list — ALL threads were removed, not just one.
column5: - ≥2 conversation threads exist for the pathway.
